speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent. Tell me, when did you first notice this breast mass, and has it changed in size or shape since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Has the mass been associated with any pain, skin changes like dimpling or redness, or nipple discharge since you first noticed it? Also, have you noticed any swollen lumps in your armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying. Given the rapid growth, are you currently experiencing any fever, chills, or night sweats? Also, have you had this mass evaluated with an ultrasound or mammogram yet?

REQUEST TEST: Mammogram, Ultrasound_Breast, CBC, CRP
REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Breast_Imaging

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammography: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast. Biopsy: Microscopic description shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth. Vital Signs: Temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Breast Examination: Inspection shows no skin changes, nipple retraction, or discharge. Palpation reveals a 6-cm, nontender, multinodular mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. No palpable axillary or cervical lymphadenopathy.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No family history of breast cancer. Social history: Non-smoker, moderate alcohol use. Elementary school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, night sweats, or changes in appetite. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the rapid growth of the painless left breast mass in a 48-year-old woman, combined with your denial of fever and systemic symptoms, I am highly suspicious of a malignant process. The imaging and lab results I requested should be available shortly to confirm this.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Carcinoma
